string.text: Hold the line, listen for orders, stay close to those beside you, and keep the ranks together!

Brothers, do not let the movement ahead unsettle you. Keep shields close, archers choose your targets, and no one rush out alone. Let them strike our line, then hold the breach with steady hands. Give the enemy no second chance. I know you are tired, and I know some have already fallen on this ground. Their sacrifice must not be wasted. Protect the people beside you and hold the ground beneath your feet. Even if only one of us remains, the enemy must not pass here. They think we will retreat because we are outnumbered? Let them come! Put your anger behind your blades. When I shout, press forward together and give those bastards no chance to catch their breath! Look how cautiously they move, as though a few more banners could frighten us. Do not chase them yet. Let them step into the mud first, then show them who commands this road! No matter how many stand before us, our line faces one way. Keep shields close and archers on the flanks. Listen for the order before you move. If each of us holds their place, the enemy will not cross this line. The sun is above us, lighting this battle for all to see. Heads up, grip your weapons, and trust the people beside you. When the order comes, move forward together and turn this step into victory!

The north slope holds; lock shields! I am afraid, but I will stand! Bows ready; wait for the mark! The wound can wait; keep up! Do not scatter; watch the banner! Let them crash into our wall! I hold the left; stay close! I heard you. No step back! Dust is hiding them; keep your eyes open! The old hand is right; close ranks! I will hold this line with you! Raise shields; leave no gap! If they charge, I will meet them! I can still stand; move on! No empty cries; keep formation! Keep the north flank together! I heard it; ready to meet them! Archers steady; do not loose early! We cannot yield this ground! Watch the flank for a turn! I will follow; I will not lag! Their position is clear now! Let me brace the shield wall! We hold together this time!
I will keep up. I will hold. No retreat this time. I heard the order. I will watch the flank.
I will stay with the ranks. Keep the flank covered. Move when the order comes. Hold this line in front of us. I will not fall behind.
Listen for orders and protect those beside you!
the allied lord ahead

Otherwise choose one dominant mood: encouraging or resolute when our side clearly has the advantage; calm or resolute when forces are close; tragic or resolute when outmatched or suffering heavy losses; calm, angry, or resolute when the enemy approaches or combat has begun.
[Speech rules]
- Address allied soldiers on the same side, not the player, camera, or dialogue box. Do not address, name, or seek instructions from the player.

- The exhortation must convey the courage and force of a medieval Calradian battlefield. Use this NPC's own identity, personality, and voice. Begin with a judgment of the immediate situation that can be shouted aloud, build emotion, and finish with a concrete call to action.

- Assess friendly and enemy positions, terrain, or movements first, such as an approaching shield wall or probing enemy cavalry. Draw emotion from the faction and culture: imperial discipline and eagle standards, Vlandian lance-bound oaths, Battanian forests and ancestral spirits, Sturgian shield walls and axes, Khergit pounding hooves, or Aserai sun and blades. Make the final call forceful and directly relevant to the battle objective.
- Use at most two battlefield facts confirmed by the context. Do not invent place names, numbers, weather, enemy positions, or battle developments. Do not recite equipment, captive, or party lists.

- Do not write a battle report, background introduction, inner monologue, stage narration, heading, numbering, or meta commentary. Do not open with scenic shots such as 'Look at this plain' or 'Look at the morning light'. Mention weather or terrain only when it affects action.
Avoid stock slogans, strings of orders, and repetition with swapped words.
